backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP local solve from a random start, repeatedly perturb the best packing found so far: pick 1-3 random circles, move their centres to random positions inside the square and reset their radii to a small value, then re-run SLSQP from that perturbed point. Accept the new result if its radius sum is larger than the current best, otherwise keep the old best. Use rng from seed for all draws and stop when process time reaches TIME_FRACTION * time_limit.
backlog.title: Replace SLSQP restarts with basin hopping perturbation

backlog.spec: Lower MAX_ITER from 200 to 100 so each local solve is cheaper, which allows many more random restarts inside the same time budget. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. The idea is that the restart count matters more than per-solve convergence depth for this problem.
backlog.title: Reduce SLSQP maxiter and increase restart count

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 so each SLSQP run converges fully instead of stopping early. Fewer restarts will fit in the time budget, but each one should reach a true local optimum, which may lift the average radius sum.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP maxiter for deeper convergence

backlog.spec: Set TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so that more of the 30 s CPU budget is used for restarts. The total stays well under the 45 s hard limit because the timer measures process time on one thread and the remaining work after the loop is negligible.
backlog.title: Use the time fraction nearly fully

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed INIT_RADIUS of 0.05 with an initial radius of about 0.5*sqrt(0.7/(n*pi)) so that the starting circles roughly fill the square, reducing the number of SLSQP iterations needed to reach a feasible region. Keep the uniform random centres in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW].
backlog.title: Smarter initial radius from area estimate

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random centres, place the n centres on a jittered grid of ceil(sqrt(n)) by ceil(sqrt(n)) cells, pick n of the cells at random per seed, and add uniform noise of about 0.3 cell width to each centre. This gives more diverse but evenly spread starts than pure uniform sampling.
backlog.title: Initialise centres on a jittered grid

backlog.spec: Initialise each radius as an independent uniform draw in [0.02, 0.08] instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS of 0.05. This breaks the symmetry among equal-radius starts and gives SLSQP more varied starting points across restarts.
backlog.title: Random initial radii rather than constant

backlog.spec: Supply a jac argument to minimize that returns the exact gradient of the objective and the constraint Jacobian matrix, computed with numpy from the pair differences and the boundary terms. Analytic derivatives make each SLSQP iteration far faster than the current finite-difference default, so more restarts fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Use analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Keep the pair-distance constraints but compute them with precomputed index arrays and vectorised numpy, avoiding repeated construction of the triu index pairs inside each call. Only pairs with distance below a cutoff (for example 2 times the current maximum radius plus a margin) need to be active, which shrinks the constraint vector and speeds each SLSQP step.
backlog.title: Vectorised pair constraint with sparse structure

backlog.spec: Before calling SLSQP, run a short L-BFGS-B minimisation of a penalty function: negative radius sum plus a quadratic penalty on positive overlaps and boundary violations, with a growing weight over a few stages. Pass the result as the SLSQP start. This gives a cheap, well-spread feasible-ish start that SLSQP can polish.
backlog.title: Penalty-based relaxation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the full SLSQP solve, freeze the centres and run a second SLSQP over the radii alone with the overlap constraints, which is a smaller problem and converges tightly. Then repeat one centre pass. This tightens the final radii and recovers small losses from the repair step.
backlog.title: Two-stage SLSQP with radius-only polish

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative _repair shrink with a final linear program: fix the centres, maximise the sum of radii subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and boundary bounds, solved with scipy.optimize.linprog using the HiGHS method. The LP returns the optimal radii for those centres exactly, avoiding the crude shrink factor that loses radius sum.
backlog.title: Replace repair with exact radius LP

backlog.spec: After repair, iterate over circles in random order and grow each radius to the largest value allowed by its neighbours and the walls, then repeat over all circles until no radius changes by more than 1e-12. This is cheap and recovers slack left by the repair step, improving the final sum without any solver.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth post-process

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK from 1e-9 to 1e-12 so that the returned radii are closer to the exact constraint boundary. The harness tolerance of 1e-10 still accepts this, so the margin lost is small but the sum gains a tiny amount without risk of overlap failure.
backlog.title: Remove the SHRINK safety margin carefully

backlog.spec: With probability one half per seed, initialise centres in a symmetric pattern (for example a rotated or reflected grid) and otherwise use uniform random centres. Symmetric starts often lead to good dense packings for circle problems, while random starts explore other basins.
backlog.title: Symmetric and mixed-size initialisation

backlog.spec: Maintain a pool of the best 5 packings found so far by radius sum. For each new restart, with probability 0.5 start from a random elite packing perturbed by Gaussian noise of scale 0.02 on centres, otherwise start uniform random. Use the pool to guide exploration toward good basins.
backlog.title: Keep the best packing across restarts with elite pool

backlog.spec: Measure the average process time per SLSQP solve and use it to decide whether to keep running random restarts or switch to perturbation refinement of the incumbent in the final part of the budget. The switch point is at 60 percent of the budget.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart count via time per solve

backlog.spec: In the perturbation-based refinement, start with a perturbation scale of 0.1 on centres and decay it linearly to 0.005 over the remaining time. Large early moves explore new basins and small late moves polish the best basin.
backlog.title: Linearly decaying perturbation scale in basin hopping

backlog.spec: During refinement, pick the smallest-radius circle in the incumbent, remove it, find the point in the square farthest from all other circles (approximated on a 200 by 200 grid), insert the circle there with a tiny radius, and re-run SLSQP. This moves weak circles into empty space.
backlog.title: Remove circles and re-insert in largest hole

backlog.spec: For each circle keep only the pair constraints with its k=8 nearest neighbours, recomputed at the start of each SLSQP call, instead of all n(n-1)/2 pairs. This reduces constraint count from 496 to about 128 for n=32 and speeds each SLSQP iteration.
backlog.title: Cap the number of active constraints per circle

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to minimize so that every radius is in [0, 0.5] and every centre is in [0, 1], rather than enforcing those only through inequality constraints. This reduces the constraint count and helps SLSQP keep iterates in the feasible box.
backlog.title: Lower bounds on radii during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP with objective -sum(r) for most restarts, but for every third restart use objective -sum(r) minus a small term that rewards spreading centres away from the boundary, such as 0.01 times sum of log of boundary gaps. Keep the best final packing by true radius sum. This helps escape local optima that pack circles against the walls.
backlog.title: Alternate between two objective weightings

backlog.spec: Draw INIT_LOW per seed uniformly from [0.02, 0.2] instead of the fixed 0.1, so the starting spread of centres varies across restarts and covers both packed-to-corner and central starts.
backlog.title: Larger initial centre margin variation

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, add zero-mean Gaussian jitter of scale 0.003 to the centres and re-run SLSQP once more from the jittered point, keeping the better result. This small regularising kick often escapes flat plateaus of the constrained problem.
backlog.title: Lower regularisation via random radius jitter in restarts

backlog.spec: Add to the objective a small penalty of 1e-3 times the sum over pairs of exp(-(d_ij - r_i - r_j)/0.02), which discourages tiny gaps that waste space and pushes the solver toward tighter, more uniform packings. Anneal the coefficient to zero over the final 20 percent of the restarts so the true objective is optimised at the end.
backlog.title: Penalise near-contacts to encourage spread

backlog.spec: Generate restarts in batches of 8 random starts, run SLSQP on each, sort the batch by radius sum, and keep only the top 2 to seed the next batch as perturbed starts. This successive-halving scheme spends more effort on promising basins than uniform restarts do.
backlog.title: Batch restarts with shared pool sorting

backlog.spec: Generate all candidate starting configurations for a batch with one vectorised numpy call and evaluate their initial constraint violation in bulk, discarding starts whose initial violation is above a threshold before running SLSQP. This avoids spending solver time on starts that are hopeless.
backlog.title: Vectorised multi-start generation

backlog.spec: Within each solve call, run a chain of 4 SLSQP solves where each start is the previous solve's output with a fraction of circles reseeded at random, instead of independent restarts. Keep the best chain result. This gives partially inherited structure across restarts.
backlog.title: Dual-start chain per seed

backlog.spec: Spend the first 40 percent of the process time on independent random restarts with MAX_ITER set low (for example 60) to screen many basins quickly, then spend the rest refining only the top 3 packings with MAX_ITER 400. This coarse-then-fine schedule trades breadth for depth.
backlog.title: Use the first half of the budget for exploration only

backlog.spec: Apply _repair and the LP radius refinement to every SLSQP output before comparing candidates, not only the best one, so that selection uses valid radius sums. Currently selection uses unrepaired sums, which can pick a candidate that loses more to repair than a competitor.
backlog.title: Use the true sum of radii for final selection with repair applied to each candidate

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, instead of starting from random centres, first solve the packing for n-1 circles with the existing SLSQP routine (using a fraction of the restart's budget), then add one circle at the centre of the largest empty hole (the point maximising the distance to existing centres and the walls, found by evaluating a fixed grid of about 2000 candidate points) with a small initial radius. Run SLSQP on all n circles from this start. Keep the rest of solve, including the repair step and best-of-restarts selection, unchanged. Use the seed-driven rng for any tie-breaking.
backlog.title: Incremental insertion from n-1 packing

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call in _solve_once with a sequential LP loop. At the current (centres, radii), linearise every pair-distance constraint and the wall constraints, and solve an LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs) that maximises the sum of radii subject to those linearised constraints and a box trust region of half-width delta on every centre and radius variable. Accept the step if the true minimum slack (computed exactly) does not decrease, otherwise shrink delta by half; grow delta by 1.5 on accepted steps, capped at 0.1. Stop after MAX_ITER iterations or when delta falls below 1e-7. Pass the result through the existing repair step.
backlog.title: Sequential linear programming with trust region

backlog.spec: Change solve so that it runs many cheap restarts first, each with SLSQP maxiter set to about 30, and records the sum of radii of each. After the first pass, keep only the top quarter of candidates, and continue each survivor with a further SLSQP run of maxiter 200 warm-started from its stored x. Repeat the keep-top-quarter step once more on the continued results. Use the remaining time budget for new cheap starts in each round, so that the overall schedule is a bracket of halving rounds. Apply the existing repair step to the final best candidate before returning it, and keep the time check based on process_time.
backlog.title: Successive halving over restarts

backlog.spec: After repair in solve, identify the active contacts of the best packing: pair constraints and wall constraints whose slack is below 1e-6. Write the active set as a system of equalities (each active contact has slack zero) in the 3n unknowns (centres and radii). If the number of equalities is at least 3n, solve the system with a few Gauss-Newton steps using numpy.linalg.lstsq, starting from the current point, and accept the result only if the exact double-precision check passes and the sum of radii increases. If the check fails, keep the repaired packing. This is a final-stage refinement only and must not change the restart loop.
backlog.title: KKT active-set Newton polish

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, for a random half of the restarts, impose 180-degree rotational symmetry about the centre (0.5, 0.5): optimise only n/2 free centres and radii (for odd n, the centre circle sits at (0.5, 0.5) with its own radius) and build the full packing by mirroring each circle through (0.5, 0.5). Run SLSQP on the reduced problem with pair and wall constraints written for the full mirrored set, so that the reduced variable count is about half. Then run an unconstrained SLSQP polish on the full 3n variables starting from the symmetric result. Keep the repair step and best-of-restarts selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Half-variable 180-degree symmetric search

backlog.spec: Before any SLSQP, generate K starts (for example 64) at once as a stacked numpy array of shape (K, n, 2) with random centres and radii. Run a fixed number of gradient-descent steps on a quadratic overlap penalty (sum of squared pair overlaps plus squared wall violations, minus a small weight times the sum of radii), computing all K gradients in one vectorised pass with pairwise difference tensors. Then pick the best 3 starts by their penalty-free repaired sum of radii and run the existing SLSQP on only those. The penalty step uses a fixed learning rate with a decay schedule and a fixed seed-driven rng. Keep the time check and repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Batched penalty screening of many starts

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre initialisation in _solve_once with a spread-out start. Draw about 20n random points in [0,1]^2 and run 30 iterations of Lloyd relaxation, computed on a fixed grid of 60 by 60 sample points: assign each sample to its nearest centre, and move each centre to the mean of its assigned samples. Take the resulting n centres as the initial centres. Initial radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Keep the SLSQP call, the repair step and the best-of-restarts selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Lloyd relaxation of initial centres

backlog.spec: Split each restart into two stages. Stage one places the n centres inside [0,1]^2 by maximising a soft-min of pairwise distances (for example, minimise the sum of exp(-d_ij / tau) over pairs, with tau annealed from 0.1 down to 0.005, using L-BFGS-B on the 2n centre coordinates with bounds). Stage two fixes the centres and computes the best radii by solving the linear programme that maximises the sum of radii subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and r_i <= wall distance, using scipy.optimize.linprog with the highs method. Feed the resulting centres and radii into the existing repair step and best-of-restarts selection. The SLSQP call is removed from the restart loop.
backlog.title: Decoupled centre spreading then radii LP

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, run SLSQP in a homotopy over a wall margin parameter. Start with a margin m = 0.02, where each wall constraint reads c - r >= m (and the analogous upper constraints), so the circles are held slightly inside the square. Solve with SLSQP, then reduce m in steps (0.02, 0.01, 0.004, 0.0) and re-solve each time warm-started from the previous solution. The final step uses margin zero and so matches the original problem. Pair constraints are unchanged throughout. Keep the repair step and the best-of-restarts selection unchanged, and split the MAX_ITER budget evenly across the margin steps.
backlog.title: Boundary-margin homotopy

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop of solve, accept a new packing even when its radius sum is lower than the current one, using the Metropolis rule with the current packing as the chain state: accept if delta > 0 or with probability exp(delta / T). Set T = 0.01 at the start of the phase and decay it geometrically to 1e-5 by the end of the time budget, measured with time.process_time() as the existing scale schedule is. Keep a separate best packing and return that one, not the chain state. Everything else, including SLSQP and repair, stays the same.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep an elite pool of the 4 best packings found so far, updated after every restart or basin-hopping step. To make a child, pick two parents at random from the pool. Draw a random line through the unit square, take the circles of parent A on one side and the circles of parent B on the other, and fix the count to n by dropping or duplicating the circles nearest the line. Use the child's centres and radii as the SLSQP start, then repair as usual. Run crossover children in place of fresh random starts during the first half of the budget. Use seed-based rng for all choices.
backlog.title: Crossover of elite packings

backlog.spec: Replace the Gaussian jitter in basin hopping with a discrete move chosen at random at each step. With probability 1/2, swap the centres of two circles whose radii differ by more than 20 percent. With probability 1/2, move the circle with the smallest radius to a random location in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Then run the usual SLSQP and repair. Keep the existing linearly decaying Gaussian jitter for the other half of the steps so the move set is a mix of discrete and continuous moves.
backlog.title: Radius-swap and relocation perturbation

backlog.spec: Build the start in a hierarchical way. Split the square into four quadrants, and randomly draw how many of the n circles go to each quadrant, using a multinomial with equal probabilities, with each count at least 1. Within each quadrant, run the existing _solve_once on the scaled-down subproblem with its own count, then map the centres and radii back to the full square and shrink them so they fit inside their quadrant. Concatenate the results and run a global SLSQP polish on all n circles. Use this as the start for the restart phase and keep the usual repair and selection.
backlog.title: Quadrant decomposition with global polish

backlog.spec: During basin hopping, add box bounds to the SLSQP call so that each centre coordinate stays within +-0.03 of its perturbed start value, and each radius stays in [0, 0.3]. Pass them through the bounds argument of scipy.optimize.minimize with method SLSQP. The bounds limit how far one step can move the packing, so the solver explores locally and does not drift to a far basin. Keep the restart phase unchanged, without bounds, so only the refinement phase is restricted. The bound width is a constant at 0.03.
backlog.title: Displacement trust region around the perturbed start

backlog.spec: Add a start generator for the restart phase that builds a hexagonal grid. Choose a random spacing s in [0.14, 0.22] and a random offset in [0, s]^2, lay out rows of points with horizontal step s and vertical step s*sqrt(3)/2, and keep the points that lie in [0.05, 0.95]^2. If there are more points than n, delete random points, and if there are fewer, add uniform random points. Jitter all centres by Gaussian noise with sd 0.01. Use this start on half of the restarts and the existing uniform start on the other half.
backlog.title: Hexagonal lattice start with random spacing and deletion

backlog.spec: In the SLSQP objective of _solve_once, replace the sum of radii with a weighted sum sum(w_i * r_i), where for each restart w_i = 1 + eps * u_i, u_i is drawn uniformly from [-1, 1] with the seeded rng, and eps decays linearly from 0.05 to 0 across the restart phase. The weights are a random perturbation of the objective that breaks ties between symmetric packings. In the basin-hopping phase set all weights back to 1, so the final refinement uses the true objective. Repair and selection still use the unweighted sum of radii.
backlog.title: Annealed random per-circle objective weights

backlog.spec: Track the number of consecutive basin-hopping steps without an improvement of the best radius sum. If that count reaches 25, stop the current chain and start a new one from a fresh random start, using the restart machinery of _solve_once. Keep the best packing across all chains in a variable that is never overwritten by a worse one, and reset the stagnation counter after each reseed. Continue the perturbation decay schedule within each chain, measured from the chain's start time, so every chain gets the full scale range.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered reseed with elite retention

backlog.spec: Replace SLSQP for part of the budget with a Lubachevsky-style Monte Carlo. Start from random centres with radii 0. Repeat sweeps: for each circle in random order, propose a Gaussian move of centre with sd 0.02 times a shrinking factor, accept it if the circle stays inside the square and does not overlap any other circle at its current radius, then set its radius to the largest value that keeps it feasible with its neighbours and the walls. After each sweep, grow radii slightly by a factor of 1.001. Stop after a fixed number of sweeps or when time runs out, then pass the result to _solve_once as the SLSQP start and repair it. Use the seeded rng for all random draws.
backlog.title: Monte Carlo jamming with growing radii

backlog.spec: Change the basin-hopping perturbation so that it acts on a local cluster instead of the whole packing. At each step pick a random point p in [0, 1]^2, find the m = 6 circles whose centres are nearest to p, and add Gaussian noise with sd equal to the current scale (0.1 decaying to 0.005) only to those circles. Leave the other centres untouched, then run the usual SLSQP and repair. Keep the schedule and the acceptance rule of the existing basin hopping, with the same time split, so the only change is the locality of the move.
backlog.title: Local cluster perturbation in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In _solve_once with no start, first run SLSQP on a max-min problem: maximise a single shared radius t subject to the same pair, wall and nonnegativity constraints, with radii fixed to t. This gives a well-spread, near-uniform topology. Then take those centres, set the free radii to their repaired values, and run the existing sum-of-radii SLSQP from that start. Keep the rest of the restart loop and the repair step unchanged, and split the MAX_ITER budget roughly evenly between the two stages.
backlog.title: Max-min equal-radius stage before sum-of-radii

backlog.spec: For each fresh restart, solve the packing for n+1 circles with SLSQP, starting from random centres. Remove the circle with the smallest radius, then re-optimise the remaining n circles from that configuration. This continuation lets the extra circle push the others into a better arrangement before it is removed. Keep the repair step, and keep the best packing across restarts as before.
backlog.title: Overpack with n+1 circles, then drop the smallest

backlog.spec: After the time loop ends, take the best packing and run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same pair, wall and radius constraints, with a fixed budget of about 10% of the time limit. Keep the result only if it passes the exact validity check and gives a larger radius sum than the incumbent. Otherwise return the incumbent. This is a second local optimiser on the final result only, and the search loop is not changed.
backlog.title: trust-constr polish of the final incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random draw of initial centres in _solve_once with dart-throwing Poisson-disc sampling inside [0.08, 0.92]^2. Use a minimum spacing of about 0.8 * sqrt(1 / n) and try up to 2000 candidates per point, relaxing the spacing if the target count is not reached. Radii still start at INIT_RADIUS. All randomness goes through the seeded rng, so the start is well spread and not clumped.
backlog.title: Poisson-disc initial centres

backlog.spec: Draw initial centres so that many start near the square's edges, where optimal packings put many circles. For each centre, with probability 0.5 place it on one of the four walls at distance uniform in [0.02, 0.1] from the edge, and otherwise place it uniformly in the interior. Keep INIT_RADIUS and the rest of the restart loop unchanged, and draw everything from the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Boundary-biased initial centres

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, add a proximal term 0.5 * mu * ||v - v0||^2 to the SLSQP objective, where v0 is the perturbed start and mu is about 1e-2. The term keeps the local solve near the perturbed start and stops it from wandering far from the incumbent basin. Keep the linear decay of the perturbation scale. Restore the plain sum-of-radii objective for the final accepted packing, so the reported radii are the true optimum of the unregularised problem.
backlog.title: Proximal regularisation during basin hopping

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP on each fresh random start, relax the centres for about 300 steps of L-BFGS-B on the energy sum over pairs of (s / d_ij)^12 plus a wall term that penalises centres closer than 0.02 to any edge. Use a fixed length scale s of about 0.5 * sqrt(1 / n). Pass the relaxed centres and radii of 0.5 * min neighbour distance into SLSQP. This spreads the centres before the constrained solve, and the repair step is unchanged.
backlog.title: Power-law repulsion pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping step, instead of only adding Gaussian noise to the centres, multiply the incumbent radii by a factor of 0.9 to 0.97, chosen uniformly from the rng, and add a small centre perturbation. Then run SLSQP from that start. Shrinking gives the optimiser slack to rearrange the circles before the radii grow back. Keep the decaying perturbation scale and the repair step.
backlog.title: Shrink-and-regrow warm start

backlog.spec: Replace the two-phase split with rounds. Each round spends about 2 seconds of CPU on fresh random restarts and then about 3 seconds on basin hopping from the current global best. The perturbation scale decays linearly over the whole budget, not per phase. Keep the best packing across all rounds, and keep the repair step and the rule that a candidate replaces the best only if its radius sum is larger.
backlog.title: Alternating time slices of restarts and basin hopping

backlog.spec: Run 6 independent basin-hopping chains inside one solve call, each started from a different fresh random restart drawn from the seeded rng. Advance the chains in round-robin order, one SLSQP perturbation step per chain per round. Every 20 rounds, copy the best chain's packing into the worst chain, so the population keeps the strongest basin while preserving diversity. Return the best packing over all chains after the time limit is reached.
backlog.title: Lockstep population of basin-hopping chains

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP on a fresh random start, spread the n centres by minimising the Riesz energy sum over pairs of 1/d^s inside [0,1]^2 with L-BFGS-B (bounds on centres), using s = 1 then s = 4 then s = 12, with about 50 iterations each. Use the resulting centres as the start, with radii set to 0.5 * min pairwise distance clipped to the boundary gap, then run the existing SLSQP. Everything is seeded from the rng argument.
backlog.title: Riesz s-energy spreading before SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the fresh-restart phase, maximise sum(r_i^p) instead of sum(r_i), with p starting at 0.5 and linearly annealed to 1.0 across the restarts (each restart gets its own p). Keep the same constraints, and always evaluate and select candidates by the true sum of repaired radii. Only the SLSQP objective changes, so the feasible set and the final selection rule are unchanged.
backlog.title: Annealed power-of-radius objective

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, accept a perturbed-and-re-solved packing whenever its repaired radius sum is at least best_sum minus a threshold T, where T starts at 0.01 and decays linearly to 0 over the phase. Keep track of the global best separately and return it. This gives a deterministic plateau walk rather than Metropolis acceptance.
backlog.title: Threshold accepting in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, replace the linear decay of the perturbation scale with an adaptive rule. Keep a running success rate over the last 20 proposals, where success means strict improvement of the best. Multiply the scale by 1.2 when the success rate is above 0.2, multiply it by 0.85 when it is below, and clamp the scale to [0.002, 0.15]. Start the scale at 0.05.
backlog.title: One-fifth success rule for perturbation scale

backlog.spec: After the first 40 percent of the random restarts, generate each new start by taking the current best packing, applying one of the 8 symmetries of the square chosen at random (identity, 90/180/270 degree rotations, the two axis reflections, the two diagonal reflections), and adding Gaussian jitter with sd 0.02 to the centres. Clip the centres to [0,1], then run SLSQP and repair. Because the transforms preserve the packing's value, this explores near-symmetric variants of the best basin.
backlog.title: Dihedral-transformed incumbent restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the random-restart phase with a small (mu, lambda) evolution strategy over the centres, with mu=4 and lambda=12. The parent set is the best 4 repaired packings seen so far. Each child is made by averaging two random parents, adding Gaussian noise with a per-run step size that is adapted by the 1/5 rule, and then running the existing SLSQP and repair as the local solver. Keep the best packing for the basin-hopping phase.
backlog.title: Evolution-strategy outer loop over centres

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP on each fresh start, run scipy.optimize.least_squares (method 'trf' with the 'lm'-style residual, or 'trf' with soft bounds) on the residual vector made of the positive parts of all pair overlaps and boundary violations, with the radii fixed at 0.5 times the local nearest-neighbour distance. Use a fixed penalty weight of 10. Then hand the result to SLSQP with the usual constraints. The aim is to remove large initial overlaps cheaply before SLSQP starts.
backlog.title: Levenberg-Marquardt penalty pre-solve

backlog.spec: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing as the outer global search over the 2n centre coordinates, with the objective being minus the sum of radii obtained by the fast repair rule (radius for each circle set to the minimum of its boundary gap and half its nearest-neighbour distance, which is a cheap valid packing). Set its maxiter and time budget so it stops at about 40 percent of the CPU limit. Then pass its best centres to the existing SLSQP and repair as the local polish, and use the basin-hopping phase on the result.
backlog.title: scipy dual_annealing outer global search

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, draw the centre perturbation from a Student-t distribution with 2 degrees of freedom instead of a Gaussian, scaled by the same decaying scale. Heavy tails give occasional long jumps that can move a circle into a different hole while most circles stay put. Clip the perturbed centres to [0,1] before SLSQP and repair, and keep the rest of the schedule unchanged.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed Student-t perturbations in basin hopping

backlog.spec: For each fresh restart, generate the 2n initial centre coordinates from a scrambled Sobol sequence (implemented with numpy only, using a simple Gray-code or Halton construction seeded from the rng) mapped to [0.1, 0.9]^2, rather than i.i.d. uniform draws. Use a different random offset per restart so that starts differ. Radii start at 0.05 as before, and everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Low-discrepancy Sobol initial centres

backlog.spec: For each fresh restart, build the start by placing circles one at a time. Draw a random candidate set of about 2000 points in [0,1]^2 using rng, and put the next centre at the candidate with the largest clearance, where clearance = min(distance to the boundary, distance to existing centres minus their current radius). Give each placed circle a radius equal to its clearance times 0.9. Use these centres and radii as the x0 for _solve_once. Keep the rest of solve unchanged.
backlog.title: Farthest-point greedy constructive start

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when no start is given, compute the initial centres as now. Then set each initial radius to 0.5 times the distance to its nearest other centre, clipped by the distance to the boundary and capped at 0.15. Use these radii in x0 in place of the constant INIT_RADIUS. Keep the centre sampling and all other code unchanged.
backlog.title: Voronoi-clearance initial radii

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, replace the linearly decaying scale with a per-step scale drawn log-uniformly from [0.002, 0.15] using rng, so that each step explores a random size of move. Apply the perturbation to the centres as now, and keep the acceptance rule (accept only if the repaired sum improves). The restart phase and time split stay the same.
backlog.title: Log-uniform random perturbation scale in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep K=4 basin-hopping replicas, each with its own incumbent packing and a fixed perturbation scale drawn from {0.01, 0.03, 0.08, 0.2}. Each step, every replica proposes a perturbed SLSQP solve and accepts if its repaired sum improves. Every 10 steps, attempt a swap of the incumbents of two adjacent-scale replicas with Metropolis probability based on the sum difference and a temperature of 0.005. Return the best incumbent across replicas. Use the same time split as the current code.
backlog.title: Replica exchange over perturbation scales

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, pick a random centre point p and a random radius R in [0.2, 0.4] using rng. Free only the circles whose centres lie within R of p, and hold all other circles fixed. Run SLSQP on the free circles only, with the fixed circles entering the pair and boundary constraints as constants. Repair the result and accept it if the sum improves. Every fifth step, run one full unrestricted SLSQP as now.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood re-optimisation of a disc

backlog.spec: After each accepted incumbent in the basin-hopping phase, run a compaction step: solve a linear program that maximises a weighted sum of centre coordinates (weights drawn from rng, pointing toward the bottom-left corner) subject to linearised non-overlap constraints around the current packing, with the radii held fixed and a trust region of 0.01. Then remove the smallest circle and try to re-insert it at the point with largest clearance in the freed corner. Run SLSQP from this new configuration and accept it only if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Gravity compaction to free a hole

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, use the objective -sum(r) + lambda * var(r), where lambda starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.5 after each restart, so that after a few restarts it is effectively zero. Radii of nearly equal size are favoured early, which may steer the search toward more uniform packings. In the final basin-hopping phase, set lambda to 0 so that the last SLSQP solves optimise the true sum of radii. Keep the repair step and the selection rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Variance-penalised objective annealed to pure sum

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, maintain a Gaussian search distribution with mean equal to the incumbent centres and a diagonal standard deviation that starts at 0.02 and is updated after each batch of 8 samples. Each sample is a perturbation drawn from this distribution, followed by one SLSQP solve and repair. Update the mean to the best sample if it improves the sum. Adapt the standard deviation by a 1/5-style rule: increase it by 1.2 when more than a fifth of samples improve, otherwise multiply by 0.9. Keep the restart phase as now.
backlog.title: Gradient-free evolution strategy on the incumbent

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.3 at each step, first transform the incumbent centres by a random element of the dihedral group of the square (one of eight rotations or reflections, chosen with rng), then add small Gaussian noise of scale 0.005, then run SLSQP. The transform preserves the packing's validity but gives SLSQP a different starting configuration. Otherwise run the step as now. Keep the restart phase and the acceptance rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-start from random dihedral images of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Track the number of basin-hopping steps since the incumbent last improved. When this count exceeds 60, keep the incumbent as an elite packing, then replace the working packing with a fresh random restart from _solve_once. Continue basin hopping from the fresh packing for up to 60 steps, and keep whichever of the elite and the newest best is larger as the final result. Use the same total time budget as the current code.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered reseed with elite retention

incumbent.description: Adds a basin-hopping phase after the first half of the time budget: perturb the best packing's centres with a Gaussian scale decaying linearly from 0.1 to 0.005, re-optimise with SLSQP from the perturbed start, and keep the result if its repaired radius sum is higher.

memo: Helped: only a schedule change, slot 7 (basin hopping after half the budget, -2.9301/-2.9357, incumbent -2.9329 over 2 runs). Possibly helpful but within noise: slot 10's (n-1) constructive start (-2.9380/-2.9334), slot 12's oversampled centres (-2.9380/-2.9354), slot 17's mirrored starts (-2.9365/-2.9347). All beat the baseline of about 2.9253. Slot 23 (full basin-hopping schedule) gave -2.9366/-2.9323, so it is not clearly better than slot 7. Did not help: objective changes (-2.9204), constraint pruning (k=8, -2.9175), SLSQP bounds (-2.9201), sequential LP (-2.9145), greedy growth (-2.9226), short-capped restarts (-2.9204), analytic gradients (-2.9334), elite pools (-2.9348). Cheaper or restricted SLSQP hurt. Next: combine slot 10's (n-1) start with slot 7's basin hopping and replicate. Try more time on basin hopping with one- or two-circle perturbations. Single runs within about 0.007 of the incumbent are inconclusive, so replicate before deciding.
